title: Is Mathematics Over, or Just Graduating?
author: Christian Szegedy

metaphors.title: Unmapped jungle
metaphors.paraphrase: Pure mathematics as lifelong exploration of a wilderness harder than the Darién Gap: mapping terrain, finding resources to fund expeditions, building gadgets.

metaphors.title: Rocks that become mountains
metaphors.paraphrase: Conjectures are rocks climbed mostly to test climbing tools; rarely one turns out to be a majestic mountain with a view over the whole terrain.

metaphors.title: Flags planted on rocks
metaphors.paraphrase: AI labs proudly planted flags on rocks explorers were already close to summiting, which upset the explorers.

metaphors.title: Satellites and mining
metaphors.paraphrase: Cheap planes bring satellites that map the whole terrain for deposits; extraction will be messy and corporate.

metaphors.title: Wright brothers' airplane
metaphors.paraphrase: AI in mathematics is at the twelve-second-flight stage: primitive, expensive, improving fast. Don't bet against the airplane.

metaphors.title: Graduation
metaphors.paraphrase: Mathematics is about to graduate; the emptiness after the last competition.
